chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We said, 'Is the testimony of women permissible regarding the legal penalties (Hudud)?' He said, 'Regarding killing alone.' Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The blood of a Muslim man is not invalidated.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women valid in Islamic legal penalties (Hudud) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic debate on women's testimony in Hudud by citing Imam Ali’s principle that a Muslim’s blood is not easily invalidated, thereby supporting the acceptance of their testimony in homicide cases. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving life and the reliability of female witnesses in specific legal contexts, distinguishing this ruling from other penal categories.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj and Muhammad Bin Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

We said, ‘Is a testimony of the women allowed regarding the legal penalties (Hadd)?’ So heasws said: ‘Regarding the killing alone. Aliasws was saying: ‘The blood of a Muslim person would not be invalidated’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran who has narrated the following: “We asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if testimony of women is acceptable in penalty cases.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Only in murder cases it is acceptable. ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “The blood (life) of a Muslim cannot be invalidated.’””
